newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money drops for the fourth day.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money drops for the fourth day.

text.p: * Rates seen rising slightly next week
Philippine interbank call loan rates slipped for the fourth straight day on Friday due to ample cash in the system, traders said.

"But I expect overnight money to rise slightly next week on prospects of more withdrawals for the Christmas holidays and window-dressing by banks and other corporate accounts," said a trader in a major Philippine bank.
The day's average slid to 10.8125 percent from Thursday's 10.84375.
"Major banks were still liquid so the market was generally quiet," said a trader in a foreign-owned bank.
Done rates hit a high of 11 percent and low of 10.694 percent.
Volume edged up to 26.466 billion pesos from 24.986 billion, with borrowers outpacing gainers 29 to 24.
Secondary trading in government securities was also sluggish.

A Reuter survey of six banks showed bids for three-month bills were pegged at 11.5 to 11.7 percent and offered at 11.375 to 11.475 percent while bids for six-month bills ranged betweeb 11.8 to 11.95 percent and offered at 11.6 to 11.85 percent
Bids for one-year bills ranged between 12.15 and 12.3 percent and offered at 12 to 12.1 percent.
